description:
hitomi.la gallery page as the DOM after its JavaScript ran (gallery.js filled the template from ltn.gold-usergeneratedcontent.net/galleries/.js). Info block: div.gallery.dj-gallery with h1#gallery-brand > a (clean title, no bracket groups), h2#artists > ul.comma-list (two artists), div.gallery-info table whose FIRST CELL is the label (Group / Type / Language / Series / Characters / Tags, no colons), tag links /tag/female%3Abig%20breasts-all.html whose text is 'big breasts ♀' (namespace only in the URL, gender only as a symbol), un-namespaced tags (/tag/full%20color-all.html), and span.date in hitomi's raw 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS-06' form. The cover sits in a sibling div.cover-column (before the info block in source order) as with an avif and a protocol-relative webpbigtn ; expected cover is that img src made https. The same column holds two more

elements ('Read Online', 'Download') that are buttons, not titles. Thumbnail strip: first six lazyloaded, the rest class=lazyload with only data-src/data-srcset; the page count is NOT stated anywhere (thumbnails are paged by simplePager), so no pages expectation. Noise: navbar with format words (doujinshi, manga, artist CG, game CG, image set), index links for tags/artists/series/characters/groups, an 18-entry language dropdown, search box, ExoClick ad slots, and a div#related-content with five related gallery blocks (.dj/.manga/.acg) that each carry their own h1.pencbxg title, .artist-list, a table.dj-desc with the SAME first-cell labels (Series / Type / Language / Tags), namespaced tag links, their own covers and p.date; one related gallery is by the same artist (quill uspn) about a different series. Unsure of: the exact ids on the info cells (#groups, #type, ...), whether the date is span.date or a div and whether common.js rewrites it to the viewer's local time after load (kept raw), the related-section wrapper and heading, the thumbnail path names (webpsmallbigtn / avifsmallbigtn), the language display names in the info row vs listings, and the footer; all names, ids and hashes are invented.
